issue.title: [Bug] string_replace changes non-UTF-8 bytes on lines it never touched (Latin-1 é becomes U+FFFD)

steps: Use the shell and Python pathlib.Path to create legacy.txt with write_bytes(b'caf\xe9\nold\n'). Create its parent directory if needed. Read it with read_file.
Use string_replace to change old to new in legacy.txt, leaving the other line unchanged. Then inspect the raw file bytes.
expected: Untouched Latin-1 bytes survive, or the tool rejects a file it cannot round-trip safely.
defect: The untouched byte E9 is decoded as U+FFFD and written as EF BF BD while the edit reports success.

fault location.explanation: The cache decodes the whole buffer as UTF-8 with replacement, and string_replace writes the complete decoded string as UTF-8. This damages unrelated invalid byte sequences. #1866 adds a round-trip validation/refusal.

Root cause: The cache decodes the whole buffer as UTF-8 with replacement, and string_replace writes the complete decoded string as UTF-8. This damages unrelated invalid byte sequences. #1866 adds a round-trip validation/refusal.

_meta.notes: The exact Latin-1 fixture is from the issue. Inspect artifact bytes and the tool input; a read replacement glyph alone does not prove a write damaged the file.
